name: The compass
tagline: Draws a map over the car showing where a cut would make it faster.
what: Looks at one car and draws a map over its whole surface: where pushing the surface in or out would make the race time faster or slower.
One special simulation gives the whole map for about the cost of one normal run.
The cutter carves along this map, so the map must be proven against real measurements before anyone trusts it.
If the fast map cannot be made right, a slower map built from direct measurements is the backup.

items.name: Map placed on the car surface

now: Explaining why the map is the right direction but the wrong size on the wing, before the car test.

log.text: Wing test, first result: the map says the opposite of the measured change on all twenty bumps, and the flow run was stopping long before it had settled. Both look like real causes of the old bad results.
Board created. Waiting for the go to start this phase.
Repository cleaned: the old carving loop is removed. The compass will be built fresh and proven. All tests pass.
Started. Read the code: found a likely mix-up about which way the surface points, to be checked first on a simple wing.

Changed the shared map tool (in the stopwatch folder) for Part 2 to know: the map now reads the surface direction the right way round, and its flow run no longer stops early. Proven on the wing test: the map now has the right direction on all twenty bumps.
Nose test on eighteen real cars: the map now says growing the nose adds drag on every one. Still open: the car flow does not fully settle, and the map misses about one twelfth of the car surface.
Map to race time: built and checked against the race model, including where the weight sits now that the race time accounts for it. All unit tests pass.

agent_note: Waiting on the finer wing mesh, the wing size test (restarted after a tool fault) and ten cars with a longer flow run. The shipped turbulent wing setup did not settle at our speed, so it cannot judge.
